MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The cable ties felt like a useful next choice because they could help organize the cables from my adapters and display connections, although I would probably need fewer than 100.",
    "Some computer accessories reflected my interest in practical equipment, but only the cable ties offered a clear use alongside what I already have."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "A hard drive, earbuds, or trackball might fit my general computer use, but I have no current need to add storage or replace those accessories.",
    "Buying a tablet mount did not mean I wanted another tablet, and buying an Ethernet adapter did not mean I needed a cable modem.",
    "The streaming stick and smart speaker did not address the connection needs reflected in my purchases, while the HDMI cable assumed a connection I have not shown I need."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My purchases seemed to be treated as broad interest in electronics, even though I usually choose accessories for specific practical tasks.",
    "Owning an accessory seemed to be taken as a reason to recommend a related device or another accessory, without a clear reason I would need it now."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "The specific connection matters to me: a DVI cable does not establish a need for HDMI, and a USB Ethernet adapter serves a different purpose from a cable modem.",
    "My interactions are infrequent and spread over years, so an older purchase is a weak reason to assume I want a replacement or upgrade now.",
    "Accessories that help me use or organize my existing equipment feel more relevant than new devices that require an additional need or unknown compatibility."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my interest in computer accessories but often missed the specific practical need that would make me choose one now."
}
